thread:
Elaine (RELEASES): Heads-up: planned rollout of v2.14.0 to hosted and dedicated tomorrow 02:00 UTC. Need customer-facing statuspage copy and a short comms blurb for support. Can we draft now?

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy queued by @Elaine (RELEASES) — window: 2024-05-21 02:00 UTC. Canary targets: hosted-us-east-1, dedicated-eu-west-1.

Miguel: FYI we added a pin option for dedicated customers in case of perf regressions. Recommend we prepare a pinning fallback note in the comms.

Sophie: agree. For dedicated customers we should say: "Customers on Dedicated may be pinned to v2.13.x on request during the window." Short and clear.

Support Ops: drafting statuspage snippet now. Suggest two lines: impact & mitigation. Also: add instruction for customers to contact support if they have SLA concerns.

Aaron (PM): include rollback criteria too — e.g., >8% p50 latency increase or error rate spike >1.5x baseline for 10m. That helps support triage.

Skyler: quick release notes bullets (for ops & customers):
- improved KV cache concurrency (lower CPU for long-context chat)
- opt-in quantization variant for small models
- fixes for rare memory leak in batching path

Support Ops: statuspage draft below, please sanity-check: 
```
Scheduled Maintenance: deployment of Redwood inference runtime v2.14.0
Start: 2024-05-21 02:00 UTC
Expected duration: ~45 minutes
Impact: transient increase in request latency for a subset of capacity during canary and scaling; no customer data changes expected.
Mitigation: rollback/pinning plan in place; support on standby.
```

Miguel: looks good. Add a sentence for Dedicated customers: "If you notice sustained degradation, contact support to request a pin to your previous version."

Elaine (RELEASES): Add a short email/snippet for customer comms (single paragraph). Draft: "Tomorrow we will deploy runtime v2.14.0. During the change window you may see brief latency variation; if you observe sustained issues, contact support and we can pin your Dedicated capacity or roll back the rollout. No data will be migrated or deleted." Thoughts?

Sophie: nice. Maybe add region note: "EU customers may see staggered traffic shifts between 02:00–03:30 UTC"

Support Ops: final statuspage snippet with region note: 
```
Scheduled Maintenance: Redwood runtime v2.14.0 deployment
Start: 2024-05-21 02:00 UTC
Expected duration: ~45–90 minutes (staggered by region)
Impact: brief latency variability possible; a subset of Dedicated pools may be temporarily pinned or rolled back.
Mitigation: rollback and pinning procedures ready; contact support with your org id for expedited assistance.
```

deploy-bot: canary deploy started — hosted-us-east-1 — 02:07 UTC. Monitoring hooks enabled.

Skyler: canary metrics look clean at +5m, p50 steady, errors normal. Proceeding to staged ramp to eu-west-1.

deploy-bot: canary deploy success in hosted-us-east-1 — auto-promote to next targets in 10m unless manual hold.

Support Ops: prepping the customer email template (short):
"We're rolling out runtime v2.14.0 during a scheduled maintenance window on 2024-05-21 02:00 UTC. You may see brief latency variation; if you experience sustained issues, reply to this message or open a ticket with your org id. Dedicated customers can request a version pin while we investigate."

Miguel: quick note — if any region shows >10% p50 regression after ramp, we hold and assess rollback. Logging will be preserved.

Elaine (RELEASES): agreed. Final ask: Support Ops, please post the statuspage update 30m before window and publish the email snippet to the customer comms draft channel. I'll trigger the deploy at the scheduled time.

Support Ops: will do. publishing statuspage update at 01:30 UTC and pushing comms draft now. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: staged ramp started — dedicated-eu-west-1 — 02:40 UTC.

Skyler: small spike in batching errors at +6m in eu-west-1 (0.9% -> 1.6%). Keeping ramp paused and escalating to runtime team.

Miguel: hold. Initiating targeted pin for the affected dedicated pools and pausing further rollouts. Please update the statuspage to reflect a partial mitigation (pin applied).

Support Ops: statuspage update (partial mitigation): 
```
Update: partial mitigation applied — affected Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 pinned to v2.13.x to reduce errors. We continue investigation; hosted traffic unaffected.
```

Aaron (PM): good call. I'll notify key customers in EU with the draft explaining pin and next steps.

Elaine (RELEASES): postmortem to follow, but immediate priorities: keep status updated, support tickets triaged, and prepare rollback-only plan if pin doesn't hold after 30m. Thanks everyone.
